questions.q: A quantity Q is formulated as $\mathrm{X}^{-2} \mathrm{Y}^{+\frac{3}{2}} \mathrm{Z}^{-\frac{2}{5}} \cdot \mathrm{X}, \mathrm{Y}$ and Z are independent parameters which have fractional errors of $0.1,0.2$ and 0.5 , respectively in measurement. The maximum fractional error of Q is

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Fractional error }=2 \frac{\Delta X}{X}+\frac{3}{2} \frac{\Delta Y}{Y}+\frac{2}{5} \frac{\Delta Z}{Z} \\ & =2(0.1)+\frac{3}{2}(0.2)+\frac{2}{5}(0.5) \\ & =0.2+0.3+0.2=0.7\end{aligned}$

If magnitude of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math> is equal to two times the magnitude of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math>, then the angle between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover accent="true"><mi>B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math> will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: A→+B→=2A→-B→ 

We have, 

A2+A2+2A2cosθ=4A2+A2-2A2cosθ

Simplifying we get 

2A2+2A2cosθ=8A2-8A2cosθ

⇒1+cosθ=4-4cosθ

⇒5cosθ=3⇒cosθ=35⇒θ=cos-135

questions.q: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>B</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mfrac></math>, then the relative error in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Z</mi></math> will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: Z=A2B3C4

When quantities are multiplied or divided, the relative error in the result is the sum of the relative errors in the multipliers.

So, ∆ZZ=∆AA+∆AA+∆BB+∆BB+∆BB+∆CC+∆CC+∆CC+∆CC

Thus, relative error is 

∆ZZ=2×∆AA+3×∆BB+4×∆CC

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II.

List - I (Number) List - II (Signficant figure)
(A) 1001 (I) 3
(B) 010.1 (II) 4
(C) 100.100 (III) 5
(D) 0.0010010 (IV) 6

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Rules for significant figures:

1. All non-zero numbers are significant

2. Zeros between two non-zero digits are significant

3. Leading zeros are not significant

4. Trailing zeros to the right of the decimal are significant

5. Trailing zeros in a whole number with the decimal shown are significant

6. Trailing zeros in a whole number with no decimal shown are not significant

From above rule, we get

(A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

questions.q: A body of mass (5±0.5) kg is moving with a velocity of (20±0.4) m s-1. Its kinetic energy will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy is given by,

K=12mv2

Differentiating the above equation,

dK=12(v2dm+2mvdv)

Dividing by K,

⇒dKK=dmm+2dvv

⇒dK1000=0.55+2×0.420

⇒dK=100+40=140

⇒KE=(1000±140)J

P→=2F,Q→=3F

=4F2+9F2+12F2cosθ=F13+12cosθ

If Q is doubled

413+12cosθ=40+24cosθ

12=-24cosθ

cosθ=-12

questions.q: The length of a metallic wire is increased by 20% and its area of cross-section is reduced by 4%. The percentage change in resistance of the metallic wire is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given data is 

l'=1.2lA'=0.96A

Using the formula R=ρlA, the new resistance is 

R'=1.2ρl0.96A

⇒R'=1.25R

⇒ΔR=1.25R-R=0.25R

Hence, the percentage increase is 

=ΔRR×100=0.25RR×100=25%

questions.q: Three vectors $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OP}}, \overrightarrow{\mathrm{OQ}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OR}}$ each of magnitude $\mathrm{A}$ are acting as shown in figure. The resultant of the three vectors is $\mathrm{A} \sqrt{x}$. The value of $x$ is ________ .
